Long-time Linux user (since '97) and reformed Microsoft basher here. I've been anti-Windows and anti-Microsoft for a very long time. For me, I got into the computing profession for a love of technology. In 1984 a new world was dawning and there was endless excitement over what we could do with these new "personal computers" to make our lives better. And, at the time, if you wanted the best compiler or assembler or linker there really was no debate -- you bought the Microsoft tools. There were choices, but Microsoft was the gold standard. This, by the way, was a time when the field was dominated by scientists, engineers, and technical hobbyists and the standards were high.

A few years later my anti-Microsoft sentiment began to fester and then rocket to apogee. Rock-solid IBMs were replaced by Packard-Bell knock-offs and Windows 3.x was an unstable wild-west (talking about infrastructure -- DLL's, configuration, filesystem organization). Microsoft seemed shoddy and it infuriated me to see the change, knowing them for what they could be. By the dawn of XP the epiphany came upon me that Microsoft, for all their power and potential, wasn't here for the pursuit of academic principle or purity of design -- they were here for profit (no shit, Sherlock). Microsoft had adapted and the lions' share of the market was no longer driven by the standards of scientists and engineers and technically-savvy hobbyists. AOL-clicking grandmas buying commodity hardware at Wal-Mart were the main customers now. But in 2005 I was still ranting about disturbing trends -- Palladium and TPM had emerged and were obviously not in the consumer's best interests.

So here we are at a new dawn. Microsoft is adapting yet again. We consumers are collectively no longer the customer. We are the product. That shift in paradigm (there's a 90's buzzword for you) is part of the cause for uproar here. Too many people have not yet realized what's going on and are unsure how to feel about being under a microscope. But the real reasons to flee from Windows 10 and to be very, very worried about hardware changes which are soon to come (and, in my opinion, backed by legal restrictions and requirements), is that Palladium and TPM are not gone and are the harbingers of the death of general-purpose computing. Computing is about to undergo a transformation into little more than a tightly-constrained entertainment and communications channel. You will have no business encrypting, computing hashes, searching primes, or "learning" beyond simple "hello, world' apps unless you are up to something. Are you a criminal? General Purpose Computing will be licensed first, then banned, because there will be no legitimate purposes for which you need to compute when all legitimate capabilities are provided to you by corporate and government services.

Yeah, I know. It sounds like a tinfoil hat rant but I fear there's more prophecy in there than rant. So why ditch Windows 10? This is a wakeup call and the perfect segue into a little more self-education about the digital world around you. Is Microsoft "evil" now? Probably not, they're just following the money in a changing world like they've always done, which will include some pretty shitty and slimey corporate behavior. That's just greed and not necessarily aligned with evil. That was my epiphany. But I do miss the company that made M80.

That company and those times are gone. However, I am not willing to give up the enjoyment and challenges of my profession and my hobby. I prefer a computing platform over which I have the ultimate control and authority. If you share that sentiment for those reasons alone now is the time to make the step. Switch to Linux and enjoy it while you can.
